Abstract. This observational review pools 14 cohort studies examining daily nicotine exposure and incident coronary heart disease. After adjustment for age, sex, and blood pressure, regular nicotine use was associated with a substantially higher rate of heart disease (pooled relative risk 1.72, 95% CI 1.48–2.01). Several studies reported a dose–response relationship. The authors conclude that the evidence strongly suggests a correlation between nicotine exposure and heart disease, while noting that residual confounding cannot be excluded.
